chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from al-Asam, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say regarding the animal: when its owners release it, or if they are unable to provide its fodder or expenses, then it belongs to the one who revives it.

He (peace be upon him) said: And Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who left his animal in a pasture, saying: If he left it in a place with fodder, water, and security, then it is for him; he may take it whenever he wishes. But if he left it in a place without fodder and without water, then it belongs to the one who revives it.

key_terms.أَحْيَاهَا: Revived it (took care of it/sustained it)
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for an abandoned animal that is found by someone else?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'ihya' (revival) for livestock, mirroring the concept of 'ihya al-mawat' (reviving dead land) in Shia jurisprudence. It clarifies that ownership transfer depends on the owner's intent and the animal's condition: if left in a secure pasture with resources, the original owner retains rights, but if abandoned in a barren area without sustenance, the one who sustains it acquires ownership. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on practical stewardship and the prevention of waste in property management.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Al Asamma, from Misma’a,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying regarding the animal when it is released by its owners, or if they are frustrated from feeding it, or spending upon it, so it is for the one who revives it’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a man who neglected his animal in a place, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he had left it among a pasture, and water, and security, so it is for him, he can take it whenever he so desires to; but if he had left it in other than a pasture, and there was no water, so it is for the one who revives it’.
en.sarwar: 16. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Shammun from al-Asamm from Misma’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If a horse is released by its owner or if he is not able to feed it or pay its expenses, it then is for one who revives it.’

He (the Imam) has said, ‘Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, issued a judgment about the case of a man who had left his horse in an unsafe place. The judgment said, “If he has left it in a safe place with water and pasture, it is for him whenever he wants; but if he has left it in an unsafe place without water and pasture then it is for the one who has revived it.’””
